title: GitHub open-sources Replica, an AI prototyping tool that builds from your own design system
dek: GitHub's Replica and how to set it up, what the first touch Mac hands-ons show about the interface, Baymard on where shoppers want AI, Gemini's settings redesign, a weekend watchlist and three events.
preheader: GitHub's new prototyping tool builds from your components. Plus what touch changes on the Mac, and a weekend watchlist.
hero_alt: A pixel tent and campfire under a moon between pine trees
summary: GitHub Design has [open-sourced Replica](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-introducing-replica-an-open-source-ai-prototyping-tool/), a prototyping tool that works from your team's own components and approved guidance, so a teammate's prompt produces something that looks like your product instead of a generic template. The first hands-on reviews of Apple's touch Mac show how lightly the interface adapts: macOS [spaces out menu items when it senses a finger](https://www.macstories.net/stories/macbook-pro-with-touch-a-mac-for-the-ipad-generation/), and the [window buttons grow slightly under a fingertip](https://www.engadget.com/2300023/apples-first-touchscreen-macbook-pro-feels-both-familiar-and-radically-improved/), while most controls stay as they were. Baymard's survey of 2,273 shoppers draws a clear line for AI features: [chatbots for comparing and researching, people for problems with orders](https://baymard.com/research-articles/ai-engagement-quantitative-ux-insights-2026). And Google's Gemini app now [puts every setting on one page](https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/10/gemini-android-app-redesign-update.html), a pattern worth weighing for any AI product whose settings have sprawled.

reads.title: GitHub open-sources Replica, an AI prototyping tool guided by your design system
reads.note: Designers set and approve the guidance, then anyone on the team describes a change in the Copilot app and gets an interactive prototype built from your real components, with an optional self-hosted hub for review and comments.

reads.title: MacBook Pro with Touch: a Mac for the iPad generation
reads.note: Federico Viticci's hands-on shows touch as a second input: menus space out when a finger is detected, the Dock hides at the bottom edge, and apps get basic touch for free, with deeper controls left to developers.

reads.title: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro feels both familiar and radically improved
reads.note: Read it for the interface details: window controls enlarge when touched, apps can be flicked to either side of the screen, and sliders in Photos and drawing in Pixelmator already work, while the rest of macOS looks unchanged.

reads.title: AI engagement: quantitative UX insights 2026
reads.note: A survey of 2,273 US shoppers: most want AI for comparing features and checking stock, most want a person for damaged or late orders, and 60% trust a purchase less when they know the product image is AI-generated.

reads.title: Gemini's Android app gets a cleaner side panel and a single settings page
reads.note: Google moved every toggle onto one settings page, cut the profile menu to account switching and support, and trimmed the drawer to five recent chats, a useful reference if your AI product's settings are scattered.

watch.title: Charlie Sutton on why design is the differentiator in AI
watch.note: Recorded at Team '26 Europe and shared by Atlassian Design on 23 October: Atlassian's chief design officer on what makes software stand out when every team has the same models, and how his team designs AI into teamwork.

watch.note: Anthropic interpretability researcher Emmanuel Ameisen explains how models plan ahead and why sudden capability jumps come from smooth scaling, a sturdier mental model for deciding when to trust, constrain or explain AI behaviour in your product.

learn.title: Replica turns the Copilot app into a prototyping tool that knows your design system
learn.intro: Released as open source on 28 October by GitHub Design and Microsoft CoreAI Design, Replica adds a canvas plugin to the GitHub Copilot app. Your team keeps its components, patterns and approved guidance in one prototyping repository, and every prototype is built from them, so what people generate looks like your product and not like a generic template.

skill.name: Replica (replica-prototype plugin)
skill.by: GitHub Design and Microsoft CoreAI Design
skill.cost: Free, MIT licence · models through a Copilot plan or your own provider

changes: Prototypes are generated from your team's components and documentation, with designers approving the guidance the agent follows.
The prototype opens in a canvas beside the Copilot conversation, so you describe a change, try it and refine it in one place.
Finished prototypes can be published to a Replica Hub your organisation hosts, where teammates try them and leave comments, without needing a Copilot subscription.
Because the starter, guidance and hub are open source, you can adapt them to your own product and review process.

install.where: In a terminal with Copilot CLI (or ask the agent to run it)
install.how: Sign in with gh auth login if you aren't already, add your team's prototyping repository to the Copilot app, then install the plugin. Afterwards, open Customize, then Installed, and enable the replica-prototype plugin and canvas.
install.code:
copilot plugin marketplace add github/replica
copilot plugin install replica-prototype@replica

install.how: Someone creates the shared prototyping repository, adds the design system and guidance, and optionally deploys the hub, following the environment setup guide in the repository.

learn.try: Using our approved design-system guidance and sample data, prototype a project list with search, an empty-results message and a way to clear the search. Keep it separate from the live product.
learn.take: The canvas preview runs on macOS and Linux only, bring-your-own model is still in preview, and a self-hosted hub doesn't mean no data leaves your organisation. Treat what it makes as a way to test assumptions, not as the spec engineers build from.
